title: Charles I and Nicholas to Sir William Boswell, 2 Nov 1643, TNA SP 84/157 ff. 217, 219

documents.route: Oxford -> The Hague (for the Duke of Courland's envoy)

plaintext.source: No decipherment known; Simpson (1893) prints the companion re-credentials letter, not this text.

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's blog, 17 Sept 2021 (provisional, asterisks where unsure)
transcription.notes: Measured with --digits, which also counts the date figures 1643 and digit tokens such as 6_; NOTES give 455 numeric groups for both letters against 457 measured. Four graphic signs are not counted. About 14 single-figure slips proposed, unverified.

system.summary: Numbers 20-115 are a 24-letter row repeated four times (homophones 24 apart), 116-159 supplementary homophones, 0-19 and 361-386 nulls, 160-999 word codes, plus four inline graphic word-signs.
system.sibling_key: Same type as the Stuart keys of Scudamore 1636, Cave 1638 and the Maltravers-Ormonde key (ormonde/); used for the design only.
system.notes: Alphabet row acegilnprtwybdfhkmoqsuxz; nomenclator looks alphabetical (hypothesis). Homophone maxima: 4 row values plus observed supplementary values (e 4+5, r and s 4+3).

prior_solution.where: R. Pitt, GitHub robertpitt/charles-i-boswell-cipher (commit 609ebf4, 14 Sept 2026): alphabet, supplementary homophones, nulls, four word codes

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Pitt's repository found with the alphabet; TNA references from Discovery; Simpson 1893 re-credentials letter and memorial, CSPD.
Pitt's row against 20,000 random rows over the same periodic structure: z = 9.6, 0 of 20,000 as good.
Free 24-letter row annealed for periods 20-32; over-fits at 106 letters, not decisive.
The four graphic signs are word-signs introduced inline: good, Cousin, Master, us.
Both letters read in connected text with word codes from context and alphabetical slots; transcription slips listed.
Addressee identified as the Duke of Courland's envoy from Simpson's re-credentials letter of the same day; arms shipment matches CSPD.

outcome.method_basis: Robert Pitt's alphabet, supplementary homophones, nulls and four word codes (GitHub charles-i-boswell-cipher, 14 Sept 2026) were on line before the attempt and applied to Tomokiyo's 2021 transcription; word codes were then filled from context.
outcome.notes: Read in substance; a dozen single-occurrence word codes open. Alphabet is Pitt's. NOTES say session 2026-09-16, git commit is 2026-09-15.
